text.p: Following are the main stories in Croatian newspapers on Friday.
- Financial police to introduce anti-money laundering office which will check identity of all customers carrying out transactions above 75,000 kuna, says finance minister Bozo Prka.
- Unofficial election results in the last Serb enclave of Eastern Slavonia should be announced on Friday.
- There will be no coalition with the Serb party bloc SDSS in Osijek-Baranja county, says Social Liberal mayor of Osijek Zlatko Kramaric.

- Hans Conrad Meier, director of Nuertinger Wirkwarenfabrik which invests in Croatia, urged his colleagues to take a better look at Croatian market in a meeting organised by Croatian agency for investment promotion (HAPU) in Stuttgart. He cited above average level of education of Croatia's work force and relatively good infrastructure.
- Government denied in a session statements by German television network RTL saying Croatia was not a secure tourist destination, branding this statement "propaganda excess".
- Preliminary results of first countrywide vote show that Croatian parties will rule Vukovar in the next four years. They won combined 57 percent against 43 percent for the Serb bloc.

- United States ambassador to Croatia Galbraith criticises Croatian government for its efforts to move Croats from Serbian province of Kosovo to former Serb houses in Knin area. -- Zagreb Newsroom, 385 1 4557075
